chinese_learning: 三种LSTM都在第八轮取得预算内最低验证CE；两个冻结变体最后一轮仍在下降，所以不能认定已经充分收敛。自训练冻结表的验证CE为4.3469，略低于GloVe冻结的4.3553，但测试排序反过来，CE为4.4285与4.4202；0.0083左右的测试CE差距只有单次seed证据，不支持稳定优劣结论。随机可训练基线的测试CE4.3262、PPL75.66优于两个冻结设置，说明此任务中联合调整输入表有较好的结果，但来源、trainability和向量尺度同时变化，尚未隔离具体原因。两次新LM的损失／梯度检查均未出现非有限值，训练后冻结表逐位不变。LM墙钟约171.31秒与173.46秒，原基线约199.88秒来自此前运行，运行时间差不能全归因于冻结机制。
english_learning: All three LSTMs select epoch eight, and both frozen variants still improve validation CE at the budget limit; this does not demonstrate convergence. Skip-gram/frozen has validation CE 4.3469 versus GloVe/frozen 4.3553, but their test ordering reverses: CE 4.4285 versus 4.4202, respectively. The small test difference is based on one seed. Random/trainable achieves test CE 4.3262 and PPL 75.66, better than Skip-gram/frozen PPL 83.81 and GloVe/frozen PPL 83.11. Source, trainability, coverage, and scale vary together, so this does not isolate why. Both new runs have finite losses/gradients and bitwise-unchanged full input tables. Their wall times are 171.31 and 173.46 seconds; the baseline's 199.88-second cost is an earlier run, not a simultaneous speed comparison.
chinese_generation: 在she could not之后，自训练冻结样本接help it，与基线的help repeating一样有合理局部接续，但后来her father did not have been great不通顺；GloVe接have been some to be，起句更别扭。elizabeth was的自训练样本重复an an，GloVe样本有she could it a most moments，而基线本身也有and and与语义跳转。mr darcy的两个冻结样本都紧接bennet，混淆人物姓名；自训练还重复her her与逗号，GloVe出现had been been。三个设置都能生成小说人物或场景相关词，却未保持可靠语法和一致叙述，并均有unk。较低PPL没有让基线每个局部短语都更自然，公开向量也没有消除重复和人物混淆；三组固定样本仅用于具体案例观察。
english_generation: After 'she could not', Skip-gram/frozen begins 'help it', a plausible local continuation like the baseline's 'help repeating', but later produces 'her father did not have been great'. GloVe/frozen begins the awkward 'have been some to be'. For 'elizabeth was', Skip-gram repeats 'an an', GloVe produces 'she could it a most moments', and the baseline also repeats 'and and'. Both frozen models append 'bennet' directly to 'mr darcy', mixing character names. Skip-gram additionally repeats 'her her' and commas; GloVe repeats 'had been been'. All settings produce recognizable novel-related words with grammar failures, meaning shifts, and unk tokens. These fixed samples illustrate failure cases rather than establish a general ranking, and lower PPL does not guarantee every locally fluent phrase belongs to the better-scoring model.
